summary: CONTEXT: a code review is a conversation, not an audit. Worst feedback is vague and personal; useful feedback is specific, names an alternative, and separates style from bugs.
evidence: Google 2018 surveys: #1 developer dissatisfaction was how reviews felt, not tooling. Guidelines: be specific, suggest alternatives, acknowledge what works, never make it personal. Technical bar did not drop.
Worst-feedback example: 'Why would you do this?' on require_api_key when 401 for missing X-API-Key already exists — no line, no alternative, reads as a character judgment.
Stuck-with-me example: 'Return 401/400 at the top of require_api_key so the rest is the success path. Not a blocker.' Names function, status codes, and severity.
PR is a packaged change asking teammates to look before merge. Reviewer is an editor, not a grader.
